text:
mara: heads-up — i'm prototyping a grafana rollup that shows GPU power headroom across regions + fallback routing indicators. goal: one glance to see where power-capping is forcing fallbacks. looking for quick metric/alerting feedback.

alex: sounds great. is this per-node or per-gpu? also what panels are you thinking? heatmap?

mara: per-gpu aggregated to region and cluster rollups. panel types: top section = region rollup (stacked bar for used vs limit), middle = node hotspot table, bottom = timeseries and a small heatmap for per-gpu thermal vs power headroom. also a sparklines row for recent 1h regression.

ryan: what are the exact prometheus metrics? iirc we get DCGM exports: nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts, nvidia_gpu_power_limit_watts, plus node labels with region/az.

mara: yep. using dcgm metrics + node labels. example promql snippets i'm testing:

```
# node-level headroom (watts)
sum by(node, region) (nvidia_gpu_power_limit_watts{job="dcgm"}) - sum by(node, region) (nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts{job="dcgm"})

# percent headroom per-node
100 * (sum by(node, region) (nvidia_gpu_power_limit_watts - nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts) / sum by(node, region) (nvidia_gpu_power_limit_watts))

# per-gpu timeseries headroom for heatmap
(nvidia_gpu_power_limit_watts{job="dcgm"} - nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts{job="dcgm"})
```

jia: nice. for alerts we should tie to routing fallback events in the console so SREs can correlate. do you have an alert expr draft?

mara: draft alert idea:

```
# fraction of GPUs in a region with < 10W headroom over 5m
(sum by(region) (count_over_time((nvidia_gpu_power_limit_watts - nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts < 10)[5m])))
/
(sum by(region) (count_over_time(nvidia_gpu_power_draw_watts[5m]))) > 0.2
```

mara: if >20% of gpus in a region are within 10W of limit for 5m, mark region as "power-constrained" — trigger pager if alongside increased routing fallback events.

ryan: maybe make the headroom threshold parametrized per instance class. older 80GB A100s can run closer to limit. we should join on gpu_family label.

alex: +1 on parametrization. also add a short-term and long-term alert: 5m for paging, 1h for ops channel.

sre-oncall: paging threshold should consider overall job impact. if it's only test tenant load, we should silence. can we match using tenant labels or route tags?

mara: yes, dashboard will show per-tenant contribution by joining cloud labels from routing logs. intent is to show top N tenants consuming constrained GPUs.

monitor-bot: deploy-bot: grafana/dashboard/prod/gpu-power-rollup updated (draft). dashboard uid: gpu-power-rollup-draft-2026

jia: one more ask — add an annotation when autoscaler reduces power_limit (we have an admin job that does cgroups/powercaps). correlate annotation with spikes in draw.

mara: good call. i'll add an annotation feed and an alerts panel that links to console fallback logs (pre-filtered query). also going to add a percentile panel for 95p draw/limit to catch skewed distributions.

ryan: for the heatmap, use 1m resolution for short-term ops and 5m for rollup. avoid sampling artifacts.

mara: noted. i'll push a PR with dashboard json + example alert rules. will also include a small script to generate the region rollup from raw node labels (we've had label drift between k8s and prometheus in eu-west). will post link when ready.

alex: thanks! eager to try. if you want i can load test a synthetic workload to validate alert sensitivity.

mara: appreciate it — please hold off load tests until i push the PR (i'll tag you). aim to get this in next 48h.

sre-oncall: ack. i'll coordinate rotation coverage if it pages.

monitor-bot: alert-manager: rule "region_power_constrained" created (severity=critical) — silence applied for test cluster

mara: posted PR: https://git.internal/redwood/grafana-dashboards/pulls/432 — includes dashboard JSON, promql, and alert rule YAML. feedback welcome :thumbsup:

alex: reviewing now.

ryan: quick nit — in the panel description add the prometheus retention window note so future folks know why 1m panels look sparse for older data.

mara: added. thanks all.
